subject: Computer Networking
title: Security Monitoring and Logging
description: One-minute skill: Security Monitoring and Logging.

hook.text: If a tree falls in the forest with no one around, does it make a sound? If a breach happens with no logs, did it happen?

buildup.text: Logs record every login, access, change, and error. They're the forensic trail investigators follow after a breach.

discovery.text: SIEM tools aggregate logs from firewalls, servers, and apps into one dashboard. Correlations reveal hidden patterns.

twist.text: Attackers often delete logs to cover their tracks. Sending logs to a separate, hardened system defeats that tactic.

climax.text: Real-time alerting catches suspicious activity as it happens — a login from two countries in ten minutes, for example.

punchline.text: You can't protect what you can't see. Logs are your eyes.

quiz.question: Why should logs be stored on a separate system?
options: To prevent attackers from deleting them to cover their tracks
To make logs load faster in a browser
To reduce the cost of storage

details.summary: Security monitoring collects and analyzes logs from firewalls, servers, applications, and endpoints to detect threats in real time. SIEM systems centralize logs, correlate events across sources, and generate alerts for suspicious patterns. Without monitoring, breaches go undetected for months.
details.whyItMatters: Detection speed determines breach impact. Organizations that detect breaches in days save millions compared to those that take months. Centralized monitoring is the key to fast detection.
takeaways: SIEM systems centralize and correlate logs from all sources
Real-time alerting detects security incidents as they happen
Log retention enables forensic investigation after incidents

faq.question: What is a SIEM system?
faq.answer: Security Information and Event Management systems collect logs from across the network, normalize them into a common format, correlate events across sources, and apply rules to detect threats. They provide dashboards, alerts, and forensic investigation tools.

faq.question: What should be logged for security monitoring?
faq.answer: Log authentication events, privilege changes, firewall decisions, network flow data, DNS queries, endpoint activity, and application errors. Focus on events that indicate reconnaissance, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.
